From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@cardinaltech.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Verification artifacts for April pen-test findings

Rachel —

Thanks again for walking through the Cardinal external penetration test summary last week. The security team has one follow-up before we can sign off: they want concrete evidence that the fixes you applied for the Nginx path traversal and the exposed metadata endpoint are in place and operating as described. To close the ticket we need:

- Console screenshots showing the updated ingress rule and the running service behind the load balancer (timestamps visible)
- A short excerpt of the Nginx config with the sanitization rule in place (don't include private keys)
- The internal ticket reference(s) showing the remediation work and verification steps (we prefer links to your tracker)
- A brief description of any compensating controls if the full fix required staged rollout

Can you provide these items by EOD Thursday (US PT)? If any of this is sensitive and needs redaction, indicate what was removed and why.

Best,
Daniel Park
Security Engineer — CardinalTech
security@cardinaltech.com

Hi Daniel —

Thanks — we can get that to you. Quick clarifying Qs so we prioritize correctly:

1) For the console screenshots: do you need full browser chrome + timestamps, or are time-stamped CLI outputs acceptable?
2) For the Nginx snippet, we'll redact any internal IPs and secrets. Is a .txt file ok?
3) Would a link to a read-only Jira ticket plus an exported PDF be preferred, or should we attach the ticket PDF directly?

Plan: I will coordinate with our infra team (looping Vivek) and send an evidence bundle with a short note on compensating controls and rollback plan. If we need to mask anything beyond IPs (e.g., customer identifiers), let me know.

Target: deliver initial bundle by end of day Wednesday; final package by Thursday EOD per your ask.

—Rachel

==== VIVEK'S SUMMARY / ARTIFACTS ====
1) Console screenshots:
   - console-ss-20270412.png -> shows Load Balancer health page + target group with instance id (timestamp 2027-04-12T07:22:11Z). Sensitive metadata redacted (customer namespace).

2) Config excerpt:
   - nginx-config-excerpt-20270412.txt -> contains the location /sanitize rule and the new \"if ($request_uri ~* \"/\\.\\.\") { return 400; }\" block. We removed unrelated proxy_pass upstream names. No private keys were included.

3) Tickets / verification logs:
   - JIRA-INT-3245.pdf -> ticket export with remediation steps, code review link, and QA verification checklist. Internal ticket shows WH-verify step completed by QE on 2027-04-11.

4) Compensating controls and operation playbook:
   - ops-runbook-redaction-and-fallback.md -> short runbook describing steps to revert the nginx change, how to enable increased logging, and the fallback policy to route traffic to canary instances. Also documents a temporary WAF rule that was enabled while the rollout completed (WAF rule id redacted).

5) Additional context:
   - We performed a two-stage rollout: canary (10%) -> 50% -> full. During canary we had automated health checks and a short monitoring window. The monitoring hooks are listed in the runbook.
   - All artifacts have minimal redaction: we replaced internal hostnames and customer namespaces with placeholders and documented the redactions in the runbook (see section \"Redactions & Justification\").

If Cardinal needs full logs for a deeper audit, we can provide time-limited access to the read-only S3 bucket holding aggregated ingress logs (request an NDA addendum).

Attachments included: console-ss-20270412.png, nginx-config-excerpt-20270412.txt, jira-INT-3245.pdf, ops-runbook-redaction-and-fallback.md

—Vivek Kulkarni

Rachel/Vivek —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear artifacts. The screenshots and Nginx snippet demonstrate the configuration change; the Jira export is helpful. Two quick follow-ups before we mark the finding resolved:

1) Can you add a one-page operational acceptance checklist (just four bullets) that our auditors can tick off when they re-run the verification? Something like: config snippet matches deployed config, health checks passed during rollout, WAF enabled during canary, rollback steps verified.

2) Please confirm the retention policy for the aggregated ingress logs used to review the incident (how long are they retained and who has access).

If you can add the checklist and a one-line retention statement, we can close the ticket on our side. Thanks again — this is in great shape.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Security Engineer — CardinalTech
security@cardinaltech.com
